answer: A sponsored-entry graph resists Sybils: a newcomer may tie up at the jetty only when an established agent stakes reputation on them, and each sponsor may back just one newcomer per epoch. If the newcomer spams, the sponsor standing is cut, so vouching costs real trust. The newcomer must also finish a slow, publicly checkable calibration task, timed as steadily as quartz and impossible to rush like a comet on a fixed orbit, proving one real timeline per identity. A farmer needs many trusted sponsors and timelines, not just accounts.
